qt: to the Commission Marcin Sypniewski (ESN) Subject:

Farmers in Member States have raised concerns about the possibility of the origin of agricultural products imported from third countries, in particular from Ukraine, being misrepresented. This problem may arise in situations where goods, after being released for free circulation in one Member State, end up in another Member State without their actual geographical origin being correctly identified. The mere release of goods for free circulation within the EU does not alter their nonpreferential origin. In light of the above: 1.

What control mechanisms are in place to uncover incorrect declarations of origin for cereals, vegetable oils and other agricultural products imported from Ukraine and subsequently moved between Member States?
How many irregularities concerning the labelling of the origin of such products were detected between 2023 and 2026, broken down by product type and Member State?

Does the Commission intend to step up data exchange between the customs and control authorities of the Member States in order to ensure effective verification of the origin of agricultural products throughout the supply chain?
